task.title: Build a 4-player online Sheng Ji (升级) card game
request: Add a new game to this Browser Games monorepo: Sheng Ji (升级, also known as
'Tractor' or 'Finding Friends' / '80 Points'), the Chinese partnership
trick-taking card game, playable online by FOUR people together over the
network, each from their own browser. Follow the repo's existing conventions
(Vite + React workspace; new code under games/ and packages/ as appropriate,
mirroring how the poker game is structured with a games/<id>/ client page and a
packages/<id>-server engine) rather than dropping in a standalone static app.
Register the new game in packages/shared/src/registry.js and add its index.html
to the input map in vite.config.js so it shows up on the portal.
Architecture (multiplayer is the core requirement):
- An authoritative Node WebSocket server that owns the game state. Clients NEVER
see other players' hands. The server: builds the deck, deals, runs the play,
enforces turn order and legal plays (must follow the led suit when able),
scores the points captured, and resolves each deal.
- A browser client that connects over WebSocket, lets a player join a table by
name, shows that player's own hand + the current trick on the table + whose
turn it is + the running point total for each side, and lets the player on
action select and play a legal card. Four separate browser sessions = four
players (two partnerships, partners sitting across from each other).
Sheng Ji rules to implement (keep v1 focused but correct):
- Standard 4-player partnership setup: 2 teams, partners across the table, play
proceeds counter-clockwise or clockwise consistently.
- A declared trump SUIT plus a trump RANK (the 'level' card); all cards of the
trump rank, plus both jokers if you include them, are trumps and beat all
off-suit cards. Pick one consistent, documented trump scheme for v1.
- Trick play: the leader plays a card (single-card tricks are sufficient for v1 —
you do NOT need to implement pairs/tractors/throws), everyone must follow the
led suit if they hold it, otherwise may play any card including a trump; the
highest trump wins, else the highest card of the led suit wins; the trick
winner leads the next trick.
- Point cards: 5s = 5 points, 10s = 10 points, Kings = 10 points. The defending
team's goal is to capture points; track and display each team's captured
points as tricks are won, and at the end of the deal declare which side won
based on the point total (state the threshold you use).
Put the deck construction, trump/comparison logic, legal-move validation, trick
resolution, and point scoring in a pure, unit-testable engine module (no
networking) and cover it with focused unit tests (vitest): card comparison with
trump beating off-suit, follow-suit enforcement, trick winner determination, and
point counting for a sample of tricks.
Use accessible, user-facing markup (buttons/labels with real text, cards as
buttons with accessible names like 'Play 5 of Hearts') so a Playwright test can
drive players with getByRole.
In the QA/validation stage: (1) run the engine unit tests, and (2) write and run
a Playwright end-to-end test that boots the server and FOUR browser clients,
seats them at one table, and plays at least one full trick (all four players
playing a legal card in turn) — ideally a full deal — asserting that a trick
winner is determined and the captured-points display updates. Record it with
video + trace ON and leave the recording as proof.
